llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed dLazy image-generation integration, but users should be aware that it can send prompts and chosen local image files to dLazy and may spend API credits.

dimensions.detail: Network access, npm/npx, an API key, and reading user-specified local media files are proportionate for a cloud image-generation CLI, and the artifact discloses that local media paths are uploaded to dLazy storage.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install metadata pins @dlazy/cli to version 1.2.3, offers npx as a non-global alternative, and the inspected npm package has no install/postinstall script; it provides a dlazy binary that loads the bundled CLI.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are direct and purpose-aligned, but the English and Chinese trigger keywords include broad generic image-generation phrases that could activate the skill when the user did not explicitly name dLazy or Nano Banana.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The CLI persists an API key in ~/.dlazy/config.json after login/auth set and caches manifests under ~/.dlazy; this is disclosed and revocable, with no evidence of hidden daemon-style persistence or unrelated privilege use.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Nano Banana 2.0 image generation/editing, and the artifact consistently describes using the dLazy CLI/API for prompts, parameters, optional image inputs, and hosted output URLs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to use dLazy's hosted image service. Use explicit wording like “use dLazy banana2,” prefer npx if you do not want a global CLI, avoid passing sensitive local files unless you want them uploaded, and rotate or revoke the API key from dLazy if access is no longer needed.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad English trigger phrases are real, but generic image-generation triggers are coherent with this skill's purpose; the privacy/cost risk is mitigated by artifact disclosure that prompts and passed local files go to dLazy, so this is guidance rather than a Review verdict by itself.
[SQP-1] expected: The same concern applies to the Chinese trigger phrases; users should confirm before sending local files or spending credits, but the behavior is not hidden or purpose-mismatched.
